scenario: AITA for not ending my friendship with my best friend after he cheated on my sister? | Both my best friend and my sister know about my other account so this is a throwaway. I'm an 18 year old guy and I have a twin sister. I've been best friends with my best friend (we'll call him G) since kindergarten, so G and my sister have always been pretty close too. They've kind of had a "thing" going on our whole lives. For the longest time, they never officially dated for a bunch of different reasons I won't get into, but they were always really close and really into each other. A little over a year ago, when we were all 17, they finally started dating. Everything went really well for like 13 months, but then long story short, G cheated on my sister and I was the one who figured it out. He swore it wouldn't happen again and begged me not to tell my sister but I told her anyway. I was mad at him and he was mad at me so we didn't talk for a month and a half, which was honestly the weirdest month and a half of my whole life. G's practically like my brother, we've been inseparable since kindergarten, so not having him around was kinda....unbearable honestly lol After our streak of not talking to each other, G invited me on his family ski trip as a way to make amends (I've been on lots of his family's ski trips through the years). I accepted and ended up forgiving him and letting him back into my life because it was way too weird without him in it. I can tell he's genuinely sorry about what happened. He literally cried cause he felt so bad and I've only seen him cry like once before in my whole life Anyway, G and my sister broke up as soon as she found out he cheated and they're still not on speaking terms, so my sister obviously isn't happy about the whole situation. She's making me feel like shit for still being friends with G, and she doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13 year friendship over her. I know G made a huge mistake, I hate him for it and I'll never 100% get over it, but I'm not gonna let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if your best friend cheated on their SO and then felt like shit, would you end your friendship with them? No. So why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall (a different college in a different state than the one my sister's going to), so none of this is gonna be something that we even think about when we're living in different places Am I the asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding the scenario. I'm an 18-year-old guy with a twin sister. My best friend, G, and I have been friends since kindergarten, so that's a really long time. My sister and G have always been close, and they had this "thing" going on for a long time without officially dating. Eventually, they started dating when we were 17, and it went well for about 13 months. Then, G cheated on my sister, and I was the one who found out. He asked me not to tell my sister, but I did, which made both of us angry. We didn't talk for a month and a half, which was really weird and hard for me because G is like my brother. After that, G invited me on his family's ski trip to make things right, and I went. I ended up forgiving him and letting him back into my life because it felt too strange without him. I can tell he's genuinely sorry, and he even cried, which I've only seen once before. However, G and my sister broke up after she found out, and they're not speaking. My sister is upset with me for still being friends with G and doesn't understand why our 13-year friendship is so important to me. I feel like she's making me feel bad for not ending the friendship, but I don't think it's worth losing such a long and important friendship over her. I understand that G made a mistake, and I'm still mad at him, but I don't want to lose my best friend over this. I'm comparing it to if my best friend cheated on their significant other and then felt bad about it—would I end the friendship? I don't think I would, so why is this any different just because the significant other is my sister? Also, G and I are going to the same college in the fall, which is in a different state from where my sister is going, so this situation might not even come up again once we're there. Am I the asshole for not ending the friendship with G? Alright, so I need to figure out if I'm being unreasonable or if my sister is being too harsh. Let's break it down. First, G cheated on my sister, which is a serious betrayal. My sister is hurt and probably feels like I should support her by cutting ties with G. On the other hand, I've known G for a really long time, and he's like a brother to me. Losing that friendship would be really hard, and I can see why I wouldn't want to do that. Plus, G seems genuinely sorry, and he's made an effort to make things right by inviting me on the ski trip and apologizing. But my sister feels like I'm not taking her side, and she's probably feeling betrayed not just by G but also by me for not standing by her. It's a tough spot because I have to balance my loyalty to my sister with my friendship with G. I think it's important to consider both sides. On one hand, G did something wrong, and my sister deserves support. On the other hand, friendships can be really important, and people can change or learn from their mistakes. Maybe I should think about what's more important to me: my sister's feelings or my friendship with G. It's a difficult choice because both are important. I also need to consider how this situation might affect our relationships in the future. If I cut ties with G, would that help my sister feel better, or would it just make things more complicated? Conversely, if I stay friends with G, would that make my sister feel like I'm not taking her side, which could strain our relationship? Another thing to consider is whether G has truly changed. He cried and apologized, but actions speak louder than words. Has he made any efforts to make amends beyond just apologizing? If he's genuinely trying to fix things, maybe it's worth giving him another chance. However, if he's not making any real changes, then maybe it's better to distance myself from him to protect my sister and myself. I also need to think about how this situation might play out in the future. We're all going to different colleges, so maybe the distance will help everyone move on. But if we're still in touch, could this situation resurface? It's hard to predict, but it's something to consider. In the end, I think it's a personal decision. I have to weigh the importance of my friendship with G against my sister's feelings and well-being. It's not easy, and there's no perfect answer. I might need to have an honest conversation with both my sister and G to understand everyone's feelings and expectations moving forward.
